title: Abby and the Underwater Garden
synopsis: A little octopus discovers a bubble garden can be lovely even when the bubbles float away.

related_resources.reason: AAP, Young Children Learn a Lot When They Play (2022), Make your home a great place to play: leave space for creativity; no claim about sea life.
Linder and Eckhoff, NAEYC (2020), open-ended observation questions; this story is not an assessed teaching intervention.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Abby explained that she was trying to grow a bubble flower, but every bubble kept leaving.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: The plot introduces a nonthreatening fanciful puzzle, not a requirement for the listener to solve it.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: These are caregiver/education practice sources relevant to the narrative approach; they did not study this story or establish a causal effect.

rationale_citations.story_anchor:
The pebbles could stay still.

The shells could stay still.

But perhaps the bubbles could be the part of the garden that went on a little trip.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Noticing how an imagined arrangement changes invites observation and playful variation.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: These are caregiver/education practice sources relevant to the narrative approach; they did not study this story or establish a causal effect.

source_note: Original fiction; caregiver sources justify only broad age-appropriate editorial decisions, not learning or sleep outcomes, and not imaginary biology or sky physics.
